chapters.title: Chapter 13: Landmark Sentencing Cases—Gall and Rosales-Mireles
chapters.reason: This chapter explicitly teaches Gall and Rosales‑Mireles doctrines (procedural vs. substantive reasonableness; Guidelines calculation and plain‑error review). Excerpts from both opinions are needed to ground the textbook's explanation of the appellate standards, the Court's language on abuse‑of‑discretion review, and the procedural-error analysis.

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Landmark Evidence Case—Sprint/United Management Co. v. Mendelsohn
chapters.reason: The chapter centers on Mendelsohn's articulation of trial‑court discretion and Rule 403 balancing. Including key excerpts will help accurately present the Supreme Court's reasoning and the scope of abuse‑of‑discretion review for relevance and admissibility rulings.

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Landmark Eighth Circuit Precedent—United States v. Battle and Intrinsic Firearm Evidence
chapters.reason: Because the chapter teaches Eighth Circuit precedent treating prior possession of the same firearm as intrinsic evidence, excerpts from Battle are necessary to show the court's rationale, doctrinal tests, and limits distinguishing intrinsic evidence from Rule 404(b) proof of propensity.

chapters.title: Chapter 16: Landmark Eighth Circuit Sentencing Presumption—United States v. Goodhouse
chapters.reason: The chapter explains the Eighth Circuit's presumption that within‑Guidelines sentences are reasonable. Including Goodhouse excerpts will provide the precise language of the presumption, its scope, and guidance on rebuttal under §3553(a).
